headline: Premium growth accelerates as DTC mix lifts margins
summary_short: On Holding's Q2 2026 net sales rose 13.5% y/y (+21.6% constant currency) to CHF 850.3 million, with DTC sales up 26.0% to a record 45.7% of net sales; gross margin expanded 390bp to 65.4% and net income swung to CHF 105.0 million from a CHF 40.9 million loss.
summary_long: DTC strength (+26.0%, +34.3% cc) and Asia-Pacific momentum (+43.1%) drove the top line, while apparel grew 47.7%. Gross margin hit 65.4% (+390bp y/y) on DTC mix shift and full-price discipline while absorbing higher U.S. tariffs. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23.5% to CHF 168.1 million (19.8% margin, +160bp y/y). Net income swung to CHF 105.0 million from a CHF 40.9 million loss, aided by a CHF 3.3 million FX gain versus a CHF 139.9 million FX loss a year ago. Cash rose 18% to CHF 1,205.6 million. On raised full-year gross margin guidance to at least 65.0% (from 64.5%), reiterated adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 19.5-20.0%, and now frames net sales guidance as CHF 3.47-3.56 billion.

drivers.explanation: Premium DTC-led growth continued across all regions with full-price discipline; management called it 'another quarter of exceptional profitability' while raising FY2026 gross-margin guidance and reiterating EBITDA-margin guidance.
DTC net sales rose 26.0% (34.3% cc) to a record 45.7% of the mix, outpacing wholesale's 4.8% growth; Asia-Pacific grew 43.1% and apparel 47.7%, broadening growth beyond core footwear.
Expansion reflects the DTC mix shift, operational efficiencies, and full-price discipline, while fully absorbing higher U.S. import tariffs and excluding any tariff refunds.
Y/y expansion tracks gross-margin gains and DTC leverage; margin eased versus Q1's implied 20.9%, a move not addressed in the release.
Swing to profit tracks the improved operating result (CHF 119.4M vs 92.8M) and a CHF 3.3M foreign-exchange gain versus a CHF 139.9M loss a year earlier, per the income statement.
Tracks the adjusted net income improvement and flips from a loss y/y; the q/q dip versus Q1's implied CHF 0.37 is not explained in the release.
Increase reflects CHF 255.0M of operating cash inflow (vs CHF 89.1M a year earlier), partly offset by capex, lease payments and interest paid, per the cash-flow statement.
Company states DTC reached 'a new second-quarter high of 45.7% of net sales' on channel mix shift toward owned stores and e-commerce.
